title: A Uniform for the Atlas
premise: In 1918, in a neutral border city where armistice negotiators gather, Theo Okafor — a Nigerian-born apprentice clockmaker passing as a local — is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock. There he meets a stranger clutching letters in the unmistakable handwriting of a soldier officially declared dead, letters that could prove the 'corpse' is alive and being erased to protect a negotiator's reputation. Theo, who knows intimately what it means to have one's name miswritten, must smuggle the letters past three checkpoints before the armistice signing seals the record forever. He succeeds at terrible cost — the stranger is caught covering his escape — but the letters reach the delegation, and Theo signs his own true name to the testimony, choosing belonging over safety.
about_author: Elodie Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the unclaimed letters of wartime postal dead-letters offices. She writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Clock That Lost a Minute
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Summoned to the observatory, Theo repairs the master clock while keeping his head down and his accent carefully flattened. He notices a stranger watching him from the gallery — a gaunt man clutching a satchel. When the clock strikes and stutters, the stranger flinches as if at gunfire. Emotional beat: Theo's practiced invisibility begins to crack as he recognizes a fellow man pretending not to tremble.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Dead
chapters.summary: The stranger, Emil, corners Theo and shows him letters from his brother Jakob — officially dead for two years, yet written weeks ago, describing a prisoner camp the armistice negotiators insist doesn't exist. Theo's POV, with the emotional beat of recognition: he has spent his life being misnamed, and now holds proof of a man being unwritten entirely. He agrees to carry the letters to the delegation — a decision made with his hands before his head consents.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, interleaved with the clock's ticking as a countdown to the signing. He smuggles the letters sewn into clock parts through a gendarme checkpoint, a delegation clerk, and finally the observatory guard — each pass costing more nerve, each near-discovery sharpening his fear. At the third checkpoint, guards seize Emil, who shouts to draw attention from Theo. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into resolve; Theo runs not away but toward the signing hall.

chapters.title: A Name Signed in Ink
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Inside the hall as the armistice is read, Theo slips the letters to a junior delegate and, when challenged, speaks his full true name aloud for the first time in years — Okafor, of Lagos — claiming the testimony as his own. The record is amended; Jakob's file reopens. Theo returns to the observatory and sets the master clock right, no longer hiding. Emotional beat: grief for Emil balanced by the hard-won relief of belonging to his own name.
